text.p: The pound scorched to a new five-year high against the mark, bonds slumped and shares fizzled after Labour's first budget in 18 years failed to erase speculation that British interest rates were heading higher.
"I will still be looking for a rate rise probably in August, possibly in July," said Mark Ramsden, economist at Stone and McCarthy in London.
Although Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown tightened the fiscal screws by more than anticipated, analysts said this may still not be enough to cool the sizzling British economy.
